newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy P.M. ready to put fate in President's hands.
newsitem.headline: Italy P.M. ready to put fate in President's hands.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he would put his fate in the hands of Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro if his hard-left ally opposed him in a key vote in parliament on Wednesday on an Italian-led force for Albania.

His statement to the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), released to reporters as Prodi began speaking, was a clear indication that he was prepared, if Scalfaro saw fit, to offer his resignation if he failed to win the vote.
Prodi addressed the lower house after almost an hour of talks with Scalfaro, the supreme arbiter in Italian politics.

Prodi cannot win Wednesday's vote, expected at around 1800 GMT, without ally Communist Refoundation unless the centre-right opposition bloc backs a government motion to deploy the force of some 6,000 troops, up to 2,500 of them Italian.
But the centre-right has asked Prodi to back its own, similar motion as a means of exposing the loss of his parliamentary majority. Its leaders were to meet after Prodi's speech.

"I declare now that if the dissent expressed by the Communist Refoundation group persists, I will go immediately to the head of state to inform him officially of the situation and await his evalution," Prodi said.
